es: Dirigir una reunión de planificación: proponer un calendario con futuro continuo y perfecto, discrepar con tacto, ofrecer alternativas y resumir.

teaching.en: I see your point, but I'm afraid the schedule is too tight.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu idea, pero me temo que el calendario es demasiado ajustado.
teaching.explanationEs: I see your point, but I'm afraid… = discrepar con tacto.
segments: I see your point, but I'm
afraid the schedule is too tight.
teaching.audioText: I see your point, but I'm afraid the schedule is too tight.

teaching.en: Could we postpone the party to 27 June instead?
teaching.es: ¿Podríamos aplazar la fiesta para el 27 de junio en su lugar?
teaching.explanationEs: Could we…? + instead = proponer una alternativa suave.
teaching.audioText: Could we postpone the party to 27 June instead?

teaching.en: This time next month, we will be dancing at the party.
teaching.es: A esta hora el mes que viene estaremos bailando en la fiesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Futuro continuo: lo que estará ocurriendo en ese momento.
segments: This time next month, we will
teaching.audioText: This time next month, we will be dancing at the party.

teaching.en: By 20 June, Tom will have booked the band, so we can adjust the plan.
teaching.es: Para el 20 de junio, Tom habrá reservado la banda, así que podemos ajustar el plan.
teaching.explanationEs: Futuro perfecto: terminado antes del plazo; adjust = ajustar.
segments: By 20 June, Tom will have booked the
band, so we can adjust the plan.
teaching.audioText: By 20 June, Tom will have booked the band, so we can adjust the plan.

teaching.en: An alternative is to move the party indoors if it rains.
teaching.es: Una alternativa es hacer la fiesta dentro si llueve.
teaching.explanationEs: Alternative = alternativa; an alternative is to + verbo.
segments: An alternative is to move the
teaching.audioText: An alternative is to move the party indoors if it rains.

teaching.en: To sum up, the party is set for 27 June, and the schedule is tight but possible.
teaching.es: Para resumir, la fiesta está fijada para el 27 de junio y el calendario es justo pero posible.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up cierra con lo acordado; tight = ajustado.

choices.text: I see your point, but I'm afraid the schedule is too tight.

feedback.es: Reconoce la idea del otro y explica el problema con «I'm afraid». Las otras rechazan sin tacto.

hint.es: Busca la que reconoce la idea del otro antes de discrepar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para el 20 de junio, Tom habrá reservado la banda.»

feedback.es: Futuro perfecto: will have + participio. El participio de book es booked.

hint.es: Después de will have va el participio del verbo.

origin.text: By 20 June, Tom will have ___ the band.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Podríamos aplazar la fiesta en lugar de cancelarla?»

answer.text: Could we postpone the party instead of cancelling it
accepted: Could we postpone the party instead of cancelling it
Instead of cancelling it, could we postpone the party

feedback.es: Could we + verbo base pregunta con tacto; instead of + -ing presenta la alternativa.

hint.es: Empieza con Could we y acaba con instead of + -ing.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase dice qué estará pasando a esta hora el mes que viene?

choices.text: By next month, we will dance at the party.
This time next month, we will be dancing at the party.
Next month, we are dancing at the party.

feedback.es: This time next month + will be + -ing describe una acción en curso en ese futuro. Las otras no marcan esa continuidad.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo reacciona la persona ante el plan.

choices.text: She disagrees politely and proposes an alternative.

feedback.es: Dice «I'm afraid…» para discrepar con tacto y propone usar el salón como alternativa.

origin.audio: I'm afraid the stage will not be ready. Would it be possible to use the hall instead?

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la reunión.

pairs: To sum up, the party is set for 27 June.
Could we use the hall instead?

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene un papel: mantener el turno, resumir, proponer una alternativa o discrepar con tacto.

feedback.es: Mia propone pedir a una banda del colegio porque la otra banda es cara. Tom es quien reserva la banda para el viernes.

origin.text: Tom: By Friday I will have booked the band. Mia: I'm afraid the band is expensive. Could we ask a school band instead? Sara: Good idea.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué habrá hecho el ayuntamiento.

choices.text: It will be putting up the tents.
It will have given the permit.

feedback.es: El ayuntamiento habrá dado el permiso («will have given»); las carpas las montará el grupo que habla («we»), no el ayuntamiento.

origin.audio: Let me finish my point, please. This time next month, we will be putting up the tents, and by then the council will have given the permit.

prompt.es: Completa tres intervenciones de la reunión de planificación.

feedback.es: Las frases resumen (sum up), discrepan con tacto (I'm afraid) y usan futuro perfecto (will have sent).

sentences: To ___ up, we agree on two dates.

origin.text: Ayudas: resumir · «me temo que» · verbo send

prompt.es: Dirige la reunión: escribe 70–100 palabras con calendario, desacuerdo y resumen.

answer.text: Let me propose a calendar for the neighbourhood party on 27 June. By 15 June, Tom will have booked the band, and by 20 June, Mia will have printed the posters. On 26 June, Sara and Leo are to set up the tents. At six o'clock on 27 June, we will be dancing in the street. I see your point, Leo, but I'm afraid the schedule is tight, so could we ask the school band instead? To sum up, the party is set for 27 June, and everybody has a task.
accepted: Let me propose a calendar for the neighbourhood party on 27 June. By 15 June, Tom will have booked the band, and by 20 June, Mia will have printed the posters. On 26 June, Sara and Leo are to set up the tents. At six o'clock on 27 June, we will be dancing in the street. Here is my plan for the party on 27 June. By 15 June, Tom will have booked the band, and Mia will have printed the posters by 20 June. Sara and Leo are to put up the tents on 26 June. On 27 June, at six, we will be dancing in the street. I see your point, Leo, but I'm afraid the schedule is too tight. Could we use a school band instead? To sum up, the party is set for 27 June and everybody has a task.

feedback.es: Una propuesta de calendario completa usa futuro perfecto y continuo, reconoce la idea de otro con tacto, ofrece una alternativa y termina con un resumen.

origin.text: Caso: fiesta del barrio, 27 de junio. Calendario: Tom habrá reservado la banda para el 15 de junio; Mia habrá impreso los carteles para el 20; Sara y Leo deben montar las carpas el 26; el 27, a las seis, estaremos bailando en la calle. Turno: Leo dice que el calendario es muy justo; reconoce su idea con tacto y propón pedir una banda del colegio. Termina resumiendo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase pide la palabra con tacto?

choices.text: Could I add something before we decide?

feedback.es: Could I add something…? pide turno con cortesía. Las otras dos son bruscas o incorrectas.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué habrá hecho Sara.

choices.text: She will have called the school.
She will have booked the hall.

feedback.es: El resumen dice «Sara will have called the school by Monday»; las sillas son la tarea de Leo.

origin.audio: To sum up, the fair is set for 4 July. Leo is to bring the chairs, and Sara will have called the school by Monday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me temo que no estoy de acuerdo con la fecha.»

answer.text: I'm afraid I don't agree with the date

feedback.es: I'm afraid + oración completa suaviza el desacuerdo; don't agree es la forma negativa.
